PP-B-VERBAL-000099.notes: 'all of the lanterns now dark' is an absolute phrase with no finite verb, so it can't come before a semicolon or colon (A, B). 'and' (C) leaves the lanterns with no verb. A comma (D) correctly attaches the absolute phrase to the main clause.

PP-C-VERBAL-000012.notes: This joins two independent clauses with a conjunctive adverb, so it needs a semicolon before 'therefore' and a comma after it. B is a comma splice, C has no punctuation, and D puts the punctuation in the wrong places.

PP-C-VERBAL-000024.notes: A colon after the complete clause introduces the list. A semicolon or period (A, B) leaves the list as a fragment, and 'because' (C) makes no sense.

PP-C-VERBAL-000035.notes: Being able to browse by material is what lets readers find the wooden objects, so the link is cause and effect (D). The other three signal contrast or earlier time, which don't fit.

PP-C-VERBAL-000047.notes: The steps happen in order: participants attempt the task, and then the instructor uses their difficulties. 'Afterward' fits; 'Previously' reverses the order, and 'Conversely' and 'For all that' signal a contrast that isn't there.

PP-C-VERBAL-000087.notes: The organizers expected less conversation but got more, so the transition must signal a contrary result. B, C and D all signal a consequence.

PP-VERBAL-20261022-A-003.notes: Two independent clauses joined by 'therefore' need a semicolon before it and a comma after. A and D are comma splices, and B has no punctuation.

PP-VERBAL-20261022-C-018.notes: A colon introduces the two tools. A comma (B) wrongly reads as an appositive, as if the specimen were the tools. A semicolon (A) leaves a fragment, and 'and' (D) turns the tools into things being inspected.

PP-VERBAL-20261022-C-035.notes: The phrase 'each made from a different tree species' is nonessential and already ends with a comma, so it needs an opening comma to match (B). The other options break the subject from its verb 'fill'.

flags: Option D 'dates, and,' is arguably also correct: 'she recorded dates, and, in the second, she described changes in leaf color' is a comma plus coordinating conjunction joining two independent clauses, followed by the introductory phrase 'in the second' set off by commas. Change D to something clearly wrong, such as 'dates, and' (which leaves a comma missing before 'in the second') or 'dates' with no punctuation.
